metadata.title: What Makes an AI “Agentic”
metadata.playlist: Agentic AI: From the Loop to MCP
metadata.audience: Students and mid-career learners getting started with AI

metadata.one_idea: An agent is not a smarter model — it is the same model placed inside a loop that can act, and the loop is what costs you.

beats.narration_text: This is Onyx, in for Humanitarians AI. Fellow Adwait Changan starts a ten-week series today, and it ends at the Model Context Protocol. It starts here, with a word that has been stretched until it means almost nothing. Agentic. Every product is agentic now. So before we build a single thing, we are going to define it — and the definition is smaller, and stranger, than the marketing suggests.

props.command: Define “agentic” precisely. What does an agent have that a chatbot does not?
output: A chatbot completes one turn: prompt in, text out, done.
An agent runs a loop: it acts, observes the result, and decides again.
The upgrade is not intelligence — it is agency, and agency sends a bill.

beats.narration_text: Right now, agentic gets attached to anything with an API key and a spinner. A support bot is agentic. A search box is agentic. When a word covers everything, it explains nothing. So here is the test that actually separates them.

props.title: The Word Does Too Much
props.body: Agentic now describes a support bot, a search box, and a spreadsheet macro. A word that covers everything explains nothing.

beats.narration_text: Strip a language model down to what it actually does. Text goes in. It predicts what comes next. Text comes out. Then it stops. It has no hands, no clock, and no memory of the last answer unless you paste it back in. That is not a criticism. That is the specification.

beats.narration_text: So ask a chatbot to book a flight, and you get this. A numbered plan, confidently written. Read it again. Nothing was searched. No fare was checked. No seat was held. It handed you homework and called it help.

props.artifactHeading: “Book me a flight to Boston on Friday.”
artifactLines: Search an airline site for Boston departures on Friday.
Compare fares and pick a departure time.
Enter passenger details and complete payment.

beats.narration_text: Now change exactly one thing. Do not make the model bigger. Do not make it smarter. Wrap it in a loop, and give the loop a way to touch the world. That is it. That is the whole trick.

show.event: eyebrow ACT TWO draws in
serif title 'Put It In a Loop' types on at 'wrap it in a loop'
body copy fades up
spark line settles: 'The loop is the upgrade.'

props.title: Put It In a Loop
props.body: The model does not change. What changes is that something now runs it more than once, and lets it touch the world in between.

beats.narration_text: Here is the loop. The model gets a goal. It thinks — picks one next step. It acts — calls a tool that does something real. It observes — reads what actually came back. Then it goes around again, knowing something it did not know before.

'Think' feed lights on the spoken word

'Observe' feed lights and the arc closes back on itself — the loop visibly completes
settle line: 'Now it can act.'

props.destTitle: goes around again until the goal is met — or the budget runs out
props.arcCaption: each pass knows what the last one learned

beats.narration_text: This is that loop as code. Eleven lines, and nothing clever in any of them. Pick a step. If we are done, answer. Otherwise call a tool and keep the result. Now look at the last line. A step budget. Without it, a confused agent runs forever and bills you for the privilege.

beats.narration_text: That loop hands the model three things it never had. State — it remembers what it already tried. Feedback — the world answers back, and the answer changes the next move. And a stopping rule. Two of those sound like features. The third is the one that should keep you up at night.

beats.narration_text: And here is the bill. A describer that is wrong wastes your afternoon. A doer that is wrong sends the email, deletes the row, charges the card. Six failure modes arrive the instant you close that loop — and the worst one is the last. An agent that fails, and reports success.

'Actions you cannot undo' lands as the voice says 'deletes the row'
the last chip — 'Failure that reports success' — holds in terracotta, alone
caption: the moment it can act, every one of these is yours

props.caption: The moment it can act, every one of these becomes yours.

beats.narration_text: So when should you actually reach for one? Three conditions. The task needs doing, not describing. A wrong step is cheap to undo. And you can tell success from failure without auditing every step by hand. Miss that third one, and you do not have an agent. You have a rumour.

beats.narration_text: So, the verdict. An agent is not a smarter model. It is the same model, placed inside a loop that can call tools and read what came back. The loop adds state, feedback, and a stopping rule — and that stopping rule is yours to design, not the model's. Agency is a trade, not an upgrade: the moment a wrong answer can become a wrong action, checking stops being optional. Reach for an agent when the task needs doing, when undo is cheap, and when you can verify the result without reading every step.

props.artifactHeading: An agent is a loop, not a brain
artifactLines: A chatbot completes one turn — text in, text out, no memory of acting, because it never acted.
An agent wraps that same model in a loop that can call tools and read the results.
The loop adds three things: state, feedback, and a stopping rule you have to design yourself.
Agency is a trade, not an upgrade — a wrong answer becomes a wrong action.
Reach for one when the task needs doing, undo is cheap, and you can verify the result.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the prompt. Take a task I do every week. Ask me questions until you can describe it as an agent loop — the goal, the tools it would need, what it observes after each step, and the exact condition where it should stop and ask me. Then tell me honestly whether it should be an agent at all. Run that on something you actually do. The last sentence is the interesting one — you are asking it to argue against itself. And watch how hard it is to name the stopping condition.

output: It should ask how expensive a wrong step is, and how you would verify the result.
Watch the stopping condition — that is the field people leave blank.

beats.narration_text: That was What Makes an AI Agentic — episode one of ten. Next Friday, we go inside a single turn of that loop, and find the part that is actually load-bearing. Onyx, in for Humanitarians AI.
